title: volumeSum and VolumeDissection
content: `volumeSum` computes ∑ c.side³ using Mathlib's BigOperators `∑ c ∈ cubes, c.side ^ 3`. `VolumeDissection` extends `CubeDissection` with the field `volume_constraint : volumeSum dissection.cubes = 1`, replacing the placeholder `covers_unit_cube : True` with the necessary geometric condition that cube volumes sum to 1.
mathContext: For axis-aligned cubes in $\mathbb{R}^3$, a cube with side length $s$ has volume $s^3$. If finitely many cubes tile the unit cube $[0,1]^3$ with disjoint interiors, the volumes must sum to $\text{vol}([0,1]^3) = 1$. The constraint $\sum_{c \in \mathcal{D}} c.\text{side}^3 = 1$ is a *necessary* condition for any valid tiling — though by itself it is not *sufficient* (a single $s=1$ cube satisfies it whether or not it equals $[0,1]^3$).

title: Basic Sum Lemmas: nonneg, singleton, insert
content: Three foundational lemmas that turn `volumeSum` into a workable algebraic tool. `volumeSum_nonneg` uses `Finset.sum_nonneg` together with the dissection axiom `c.side_pos`; `volumeSum_singleton` is `simp`-trivial after unfolding; `volumeSum_insert` requires classical `DecidableEq Cube` (declared once at line 52) so that `Finset.sum_insert` applies. These lemmas form the inductive backbone for all later volume bounds.
mathContext: These are the three structural properties of a measure-like map $\mu(S) = \sum_{c \in S} c.\text{side}^3$: positivity ($\mu \geq 0$), the singleton case ($\mu(\{c\}) = c.\text{side}^3$), and finite additivity for disjoint inserts ($\mu(\{c\} \cup S) = c.\text{side}^3 + \mu(S)$ when $c \notin S$). Together with `volumeSum_union` (Part IV) they say $\mu$ is a finitely additive nonneg set function on `Finset Cube`.

title: Volume and Side Bounds from Constraint
content: `cube_volume_le_one` uses `Finset.single_le_sum`: since each term is nonneg and the total is 1, every individual term is ≤ 1. `cube_side_le_one` then derives `c.side ≤ 1` from `c.side³ ≤ 1` and `c.side > 0` using `nlinarith` with the hint `sq_nonneg (c.side - 1)`, which expands to `c.side² - 2·c.side + 1 ≥ 0` and enables cubic arithmetic.
mathContext: From $\sum s_i^3 = 1$ with each $s_i^3 \geq 0$, we get $s_k^3 \leq 1$ for each $k$. Since $s_k > 0$ (positivity axiom), $s_k^3 \leq 1$ implies $s_k \leq 1$. The algebraic step: if $s > 1$ then $(s-1)^2 \geq 0$ gives $s^2 \geq 2s - 1$, so $s^3 = s \cdot s^2 \geq s(2s-1) = 2s^2 - s > 2(1) - 1 = 1$ for $s > 1$.

title: Strict Bound c.side³ < 1 When ≥ 2 Cubes
content: `cube_volume_lt_one_of_card_ge_two` strengthens the ≤ 1 bound to a strict < 1 whenever the dissection has at least two cubes. The proof argues by contradiction: if `c.side³ = 1` then the entire volume budget is consumed by `c`, but extracting another cube `c'` (via `Finset.one_lt_card`) gives a positive contribution `c'.side³ > 0`, so the pair `{c, c'}` already sums to more than 1 — contradicting `volume_constraint`. The technical step is bounding the pair sum below the total via `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg`.
mathContext: If $\sum_i s_i^3 = 1$ and some $s_k^3 = 1$, then $\sum_{i \neq k} s_i^3 = 0$. Since each $s_i^3 > 0$ (positivity), the index set $\{i : i \neq k\}$ must be empty, i.e., the dissection has only one cube. Contrapositively, $|\mathcal{D}| \geq 2 \Rightarrow s_k^3 < 1$ for every $k$. This is a discrete analog of the strict mean-value inequality.

title: Collision Pairs and Volume: 2s³ ≤ 1
content: `collision_volume_bound` proves that for any collision pair (c₁, c₂) — two distinct cubes with c₁.side = c₂.side = s — we have 2s³ ≤ 1. The proof: both cubes are in the dissection, so their total volume c₁.side³ + c₂.side³ = 2s³ is bounded by volumeSum = 1. `collision_side_le_half_cbrt` immediately gives s³ ≤ 1/2.
mathContext: If two distinct cubes with the same side length $s$ appear in a VolumeDissection, they each contribute $s^3$ to the sum $\sum c_i^3 = 1$. Since all other terms are nonneg, $2s^3 \leq 1$, i.e., $s \leq 2^{-1/3} \approx 0.7937$. This is a quantitative upper bound on how large any repeated-size cube can be in a volume-constrained dissection — and it is *tight*: two cubes of side $2^{-1/3}$ would saturate the bound (though they could not actually tile $[0,1]^3$).

title: Cardinality and Disjoint-Union Decomposition
content: `min_cubes_for_collision` extracts a card ≥ 2 lower bound from any collision-pair witness via `Finset.card_le_card` on `{c₁,c₂} ⊆ d.cubes`. `volumeSum_union` lifts `Finset.sum_union` to `volumeSum`, so the volume map is finitely additive on disjoint unions. `volumeSum_eq` is a rewrite-only `rfl` lemma that re-exposes the underlying `Finset.sum` formulation when later proofs need to manipulate the sum directly.
mathContext: The disjoint-union identity $\mu(S \sqcup T) = \mu(S) + \mu(T)$ is what makes `volumeSum` behave like a *finitely additive measure* on the powerset of cubes. Combined with `volumeSum_singleton` it characterizes the function uniquely. Algebraically, this is the universal property of the free commutative monoid generated by cube volumes.

title: Existence Witness: VolumeDissection Is Not Vacuous
content: `volume_constraint_satisfiable` constructs an explicit witness — a single unit cube $\langle 0,0,0,1\rangle$ at the origin — and verifies that all `CubeDissection` axioms hold (containment in $[0,1]^3$, vacuously pairwise-disjoint since one cube, and `covers_unit_cube : True` is trivial), and that `volumeSum {c} = 1` via `volumeSum_singleton`. This rules out the embarrassing scenario where `VolumeDissection` is uninhabited, in which case all theorems would be vacuously true and the entire structure would carry no mathematical content.
mathContext: Existence (non-vacuity) is a routine but essential check for any new structure: a theorem of the form '∀ vd : VolumeDissection, P vd' is mathematically meaningful only when `VolumeDissection` has at least one inhabitant. Here the trivial dissection $\mathcal{D} = \{[0,1]^3\}$ — a single cube of side 1 — is the canonical witness. It is the *unique* VolumeDissection of cardinality 1, since $s_1^3 = 1$ forces $s_1 = 1$ over $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$.
